subject: SLO apportionment appeal — deployment conflict and evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@clearmart.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: support@clearmart.com, procurement@clearmart.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Brief production error spike during 11/20 midnight deploy — requesting SLA relief and timeline

Hi Avery,

We saw a correlated flood of 503s across multiple checkout routes between 23:57 and 00:06 PST on 2025-11-20 (approx). This coincided with our scheduled canary deployment that rolled to ~15% of traffic for the new recommendation model. The issue caused checkout failures for roughly 2.8% of overall transactions during that window — we have the billing delta that shows declined orders and a CSV snapshot attached.

Per the contract (section 4.2), Clearmart requests Redwood evaluate eligibility for proportional SLA credit and provide a post-incident timeline (logs, canary rollout timestamps, and any routing/fallback events). We are happy to share request ids and a sample error rate graph.

What we need from Redwood:
- Confirmation of the impacted time window (start/end with timezone)
- Fraction of traffic that was affected by the routing misalignment (if you have per-region broken-down rates)
- An initial statement on whether this qualifies as an SLO breach under the 99.95% availability calculation
- ETA for a postmortem and raw trace bundle (we need this by end of next business day for our procurement), or explanation if earlier, please escalate.

Attaching: clearmart_billing_snapshot.csv (small excerpt)

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our ops and procurement teams.

— Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Operations, Clearmart
elena@clearmart.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@clearmart.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Brief production error spike during 11/20 midnight deploy — requesting SLA relief and timeline

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and for the billing snapshot. We've opened internal tracking for this (JIRA-INF-7821). I can confirm we see a spike in 503s that aligns with your window and the deploy, and we'll treat this as an urgent SLA adjudication. A few initial notes and next steps: 

1) Confirmation of window: our preliminary telemetry shows increased 5xx responses starting 2025-11-20T23:56:10-08:00 and returning to baseline by ~2025-11-21T00:07:30-08:00. We'll correlate with your request ids.

2) Trace/Log bundle: David (cc'd) will pull the KV-cache and routing traces and attach a tar.gz with request-level samples; expect that by EOD.

3) Traffic fraction & impact: we'll estimate the percentage of total traffic routed to the canary variant during that short window and produce an apportionment calculation for proportional credit.

4) Contract interpretation: Marissa (AM) will start the remedy workflow and confirm the necessary paperwork for a proportional credit (DocuSign link if applicable).

Can you confirm whether you only want credit applied to the billing period that includes Nov 20, or if you prefer a one-time invoice adjustment? Also, please send 3-5 example request ids for the failed checkouts to speed correlation.

We will follow up with the trace bundle and a proposed remediation timeline within the next 8 business hours. If you prefer a brief call today, I'm available 11:30–12:30PT.

— Avery Johnson
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@clearmart.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Brief production error spike during 11/20 midnight deploy — requesting SLA relief and timeline

Avery / Elena — attaching the trace bundle and a short technical summary. Forwarding raw pieces below for visibility.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: infra-traces@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 11:56:22 -08:00
Subject: INF-7821: collect canary routing & kv-cache traces for 2025-11-20T23:55:00-00:10:00 PST

Collected artifacts (attached as trace_bundle_20251121.tar.gz):
- routing_events.log (UTC timestamps, filtered for canary buckets)
- kv_cache_miss_samples.jsonl (selected request ids)
- runtime_metrics.csv (per-node 1s granularity)
- request_samples.txt (30 anonymized request ids and headers)

Preliminary findings (short):
- At 23:56:09 PST we see a short-lived mismatch between orchestrator target group and canary tagging resulting in ~18% of traffic being routed to a model variant that lacked a warmed KV cache for recommendations. That mismatch coincides with a 503 spike.
- Several nodes returned 503s due to downstream cache misses combined with a synchronous cold-start path in the recommender kernel; CPU saturation is visible for 30s on those hosts.
- Automatic fallback attempted to re-route at 23:56:45 PST but a small percentage of requests (~0.3% of total) continued to fail until 00:03:10 PST because of a sticky session affinity in the legacy LB logic.

What we'll provide next:
- A per-route apportionment table (CSV) mapping impacted transactions to total transactions for the billing window
- Exact TZ-normalized start/end times for the official adjudication window
- Raw trace bundle (attached)

Attachments: trace_bundle_20251121.tar.gz

If you want us to expedite a deeper RCA (root cause that will go public), please confirm and we'll schedule the postmortem meeting for next week and include the product team.

— David Kim
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@clearmart.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, procurement@clearmart.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Brief production error spike during 11/20 midnight deploy — requesting SLA relief and timeline

Thanks, all — received the trace bundle and the initial timing. Procurement wants the apportionment calculation to be applied as a credit to November's invoice (one-time invoice adjustment). We attach three example request ids and a short excerpt from our own graphing.

We also ask that the postmortem include:
- a timeline with exact deploy steps and any rollback events,
- any changes to rolling/affinity logic you plan to make, and
- an explicit statement on whether the event was caused by a Redwood routing change vs. a customer configuration.

Please proceed with the proportional credit calculation and add a proposed postmortem slot on Monday 2025-11-24 09:00 PT (we can move if needed).

Attachments: clearmart_billing_snapshot.csv, sample_request_ids.txt

— Elena
